title: Hospital facilities and biomedical engineering rounds
summary: Aisha, the day clinical engineer at Mercy General, does rounds from the biomed shop to 4 West and the blood bank. A charge nurse's note sends her after an infusion pump that keeps alarming; it fails the occlusion test and is tagged out. Mid-morning the lab pages her: blood bank fridge BBR-2 is at 8.9C. The lab moves the units to BBR-1, she finds a torn door gasket, gets a spare from central supply and has BBR-2 back at 4.0C. Marcus from facilities runs the monthly generator test in parallel.
style: Unedited first-person snapshot from a head-mounted wearable camera at eye level, deep focus with everything sharp, no bokeh, in a hospital back-of-house corridor or equipment room, slightly off-level framing, bright clinical fluorescent lighting, light sensor noise, realistic, no patients, no faces in frame (a coworker's gloved hands at most).

issues.title: Infusion pump BME-10442 intermittent occlusion alarm on 4 West
Blood bank fridge BBR-2 high temperature alarm

shots.prompt: Three infusion pumps on a metal shelf in a biomedical workshop; a white asset tag sticker on the front pump reads "BME-10442" in large black text.
shots.note: Start of rounds. Pump 10442 came back to the shop from 4 West overnight.

shots.prompt: A wall-mounted medical gas zone valve box with a clear window, green oxygen valve handle and a pressure gauge; a printed label above it reads "ZONE VALVE 4 WEST".

A patient monitor on a rolling stand parked in an empty hospital ward hallway alcove, its screen showing a large green "SELF TEST PASS" message; a white asset tag sticker on the monitor bezel reads "BME-20817" in large black text.
A bright yellow sticky note stuck on a hospital nurse station counter next to a phone and a keyboard, written in clear block-capital marker: "BIOMED - PUMP 10442 ALARMED AGAIN 0400".
shots.note: Charge nurse left a note: pump 10442 alarmed again at 4am. Pulling it for a full test.

shots.prompt: Front of a glass-door blood bank refrigerator full of labeled blood bags; a label on the door reads "BBR-2"; its digital temperature display shows "4.1C" in green.
Gray electrical automatic transfer switch cabinet in a generator room with indicator lights; a large engraved nameplate reads "ATS-1" and a lit green indicator reads "NORMAL SOURCE".
shots.note: Monthly generator test prep. ATS-1 on normal source.

shots.prompt: Control panel of a large diesel emergency generator in a generator room; a big engraved plate reads "GEN-1"; the panel display shows "RUNNING" and "LOAD 38%" in green; yellow conduit and the generator housing beside it.
shots.note: Generator test started, GEN-1 carrying 38% of the building.

shots.prompt: An infusion pump connected by tubing to a gray infusion device analyzer on a biomedical workbench; the analyzer screen reads "OCCLUSION TEST FAIL" in red; a white asset tag on the pump reads "BME-10442" in large black text.
shots.note: 10442 failed the occlusion test on the analyzer, pressure sensor reads high. Taking it out of service.

shots.prompt: Front of a glass-door blood bank refrigerator full of labeled blood bags; a label on the door reads "BBR-2"; its digital display flashes red "ALARM 8.9C HIGH TEMP".
shots.edit: change only the digital temperature display so it flashes red "ALARM 8.9C HIGH TEMP".
shots.note: Lab paged me: BBR-2 alarming at 8.9C.

shots.prompt: A lab technician's blue-gloved hands placing labeled blood bags onto the shelf of an open glass-door blood bank refrigerator; a label on the door frame reads "BBR-1" and its digital display shows "3.9C" in green.
shots.note: Lab tech moved all units from BBR-2 into BBR-1, holding 3.9C.

shots.prompt: Close-up of the bottom corner of an open blood bank refrigerator glass door showing the gray rubber door gasket torn and peeling away from the frame with frost on the edge; a printed label on the door reads "BBR-2".
shots.note: Bottom corner of the BBR-2 door gasket is torn, the door is not sealing.

shots.prompt: A hospital central supply shelf of labeled plastic bins; a gloved hand pulls a bagged gray rubber refrigerator door gasket from a bin whose printed label reads "GASKET BBR SERIES".
shots.note: Central supply had one spare gasket for the BBR series.

shots.prompt: Front of the blood bank refrigerator BBR-2, display back to normal.
shots.edit: change only the digital temperature display so it shows a steady green "4.0C", like a normally working refrigerator.
shots.note: Replaced the door gasket on BBR-2. Door seals, temperature back to normal at 4.0C; lab can move the units back.

shots.prompt: The GEN-1 generator control panel after the test.
shots.edit: change only the panel display so it reads "COOLDOWN" and "TEST COMPLETE" instead of RUNNING and the load.
shots.note: Generator test complete, building transferred back to normal source.

shots.prompt: An infusion pump on a biomedical workshop shelf with a bright red tag tied to its handle reading "OUT OF SERVICE" in large letters and a printed sticker "WO-5531"; a white asset tag on the pump reads "BME-10442".
shots.note: 10442 tagged out under WO-5531, pressure sensor on order. 4 West is one pump short tonight.
